question: A ward manager wants to speed up patient discharges. Using systems thinking, what is the best first step?

options.A: Examine how nursing, pharmacy, and transport work together during discharge
options.B: Force the nursing staff to work faster without talking to others
options.C: Focus only on speeding up the discharge lounge staff
options.D: Punish nurses whose patients take too long to leave

explanation: To fix a delay, you have to look at the whole chain of events, not just one group of workers.

question: What is the primary focus of holistic support in palliative nursing?

options.A: Preparing the family solely for funeral arrangements
options.B: Curing the underlying pathological disease
options.C: Addressing physical, emotional, social, and spiritual needs
options.D: Strictly managing vital signs and lab values

explanation: Holistic support looks at the entire human experience of illness, ensuring that pain, emotional distress, and spiritual concerns are all treated with equal importance. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h1)

question: Why is dobutamine often prescribed for a patient with cardiogenic shock?

options.A: It strengthens the pumping action of the heart muscle
options.B: It prevents dangerous allergic reactions in the blood
options.C: It removes excess fluid directly through the kidneys
options.D: It lowers the patient's body temperature to rest the heart

explanation: Dobutamine is an inotrope that increases the force of myocardial contraction, helping a weak heart pump more blood forward. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h6)

question: Which part of the ear does a tympanic thermometer aim for?

options.A: The sublingual pocket
options.B: The temporal artery
options.C: The tympanic membrane
options.D: The carotid sheath

explanation: Tympanic thermometers go gently into the ear canal to pick up heat coming straight off the eardrum.

question: If a patient loses their pulse, what document should you check right away to see if they didn't want life-saving efforts?

options.A: Patient admission summary
options.B: Do Not Resuscitate order
options.C: Daily nursing care plan
options.D: Discharge planning form

explanation: Great thinking! A DNR order tells the team whether the patient requested to skip measures like CPR.

question: When planning a new health program in a village, why is it vital for a nurse to involve local leaders?

options.A: To shift all financial responsibility onto the community members
options.B: To replace the need for professional nursing assessments
options.C: To comply with international travel regulations
options.D: To ensure the program respects local values and gains community acceptance

explanation: Well done! Working with local leaders builds trust and makes sure your health projects fit nicely with the culture and lifestyle of the people.

question: What is the best step-by-step order for a nurse trying to wake a sleeping patient during a neuro check?

options.A: Checking pupils before ever speaking to the patient
options.B: Physical shaking followed by cold water application
options.C: Painful stimulus first, followed by loud yelling
options.D: Voice, then touch, and finally painful stimulus if needed

explanation: Always start gently! Call their name in a normal voice first, move to a gentle touch if they don't answer, and only use pain as a last resort.

question: Which two vital signs usually go up when a patient has an active infection?

options.A: Heart rate and respiratory rate
options.B: Blood sugar and platelet count
options.C: Body weight and pupil diameter
options.D: Blood pressure and urine output

explanation: Spot on! Because a fever speeds up your metabolism, your heart beats faster and you breathe a bit quicker to keep up with the body's demand for oxygen.

question: Why is Small Cell Lung Cancer usually treated with medications (systemic therapy) rather than surgery right away?

options.A: It only occurs in patients who are too old for operations.
options.B: It grows extremely slowly inside the main bronchial tubes.
options.C: It usually spreads to other body parts very early before detection.
options.D: It is completely resistant to any form of surgical removal.

explanation: Great thinking! Small cell lung cancer grows fast and tends to spread (metastasize) early, meaning surgery alone usually isn't enough to catch it all.

question: How long does the postpartum puerperium period typically last?

options.A: Three months
options.B: Nine months
options.C: Six weeks
options.D: Two weeks

explanation: You've got this! The puerperium lasts for about six weeks after childbirth. This is the special time the mother's body needs for her reproductive organs to gently return to their normal, non-pregnant state.

question: Which of these options does NOT weaken or suppress a person's immune system?

options.A: Chronic high levels of physical and mental stress
options.B: Adequate daily nutrition and balanced diet
options.C: Severe protein and micronutrient deficiency
options.D: Long-term use of immunosuppressant medications

explanation: Nice work! Good food and a balanced diet nourish and support your immunity rather than harming it.

question: When do symptoms of neonatal tetanus usually first show up?

options.A: At approximately six months postpartum
options.B: Between three and fourteen days after birth
options.C: Around six to eight weeks of age
options.D: Within the first 24 hours of life

explanation: Spot on! Symptoms typically appear in the first two weeks of life, often after the baby was feeding and acting completely normal at first.

question: Which side effect often happens when drugs like metoclopramide and promethazine block dopamine in the brain?

options.A: Severe persistent diarrhea
options.B: Hypertensive crisis
options.C: Extrapyramidal symptoms
options.D: Pulmonary edema

explanation: You got it! Blocking dopamine can mess with movement control, leading to extrapyramidal symptoms like muscle spasms or restlessness. Always watch your patients for this!

question: What actually causes the noisy breathing known as the 'death rattle' in a dying patient?

options.A: Air moving past pooled saliva and mucus in the upper airway
options.B: Spasms of the chest diaphragm muscle
options.C: Narrowing of the main windpipe from inflammation
options.D: Fluid filling up the small air sacs deep in the lungs

explanation: The death rattle sounds scary, but it's just air passing over saliva that the patient is too weak to cough up or swallow. You're doing great!

question: What happens to fixed costs when patient numbers go up in the hospital?

options.A: They stay exactly the same
options.B: They become direct costs
options.C: They increase significantly
options.D: They drop down to zero

explanation: Fixed costs (like building rent) don't care how many patients walk through the door; they stay stubborn and unchanging regardless!

question: Taking which class of medications for a long time is well-known to cause bone loss and muscle weakness?

options.A: Antihistamines
options.B: Antibiotics
options.C: Bronchodilators
options.D: Corticosteroids

explanation: Correct! Long-term use of corticosteroids interferes with how the body handles calcium, often leading to bone thinning.

question: Why do people need to take the influenza vaccine every single year?

options.A: The government needs yearly numbers for health records
options.B: The vaccine turns toxic if stored for more than a year
options.C: The flu virus mutates and changes its shape from year to year
options.D: Immunity from last year's shot completely disappears in six months

explanation: Flu viruses are clever changelings! They undergo constant changes (antigenic drift), so scientists update the vaccine annually to match whatever strain is currently spreading.

question: What document lets a competent person state their medical treatment preferences before they lose the ability to decide?

options.A: Standard hospital admission form
options.B: Professional nursing license certificate
options.C: Incident liability report
options.D: Advance directive or living will

explanation: Correct! An advance directive gives people a voice in their future medical care even if they later become unable to speak for themselves.

question: Which two medications belong to the Class IV calcium channel blocker group?

options.A: Lidocaine and flecainide
options.B: Digoxin and adenosine
options.C: Verapamil and diltiazem
options.D: Metoprolol and atenolol

explanation: Verapamil and diltiazem are non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers used to control heart rates in SVTs. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h6)

question: A patient has a blockage in their intestinal lymph vessels (lacteals). Which nutrient absorption will be hit hardest?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Amino acids
options.C: Water
options.D: Lipids

explanation: Remember that dietary fats are too chunky for regular blood capillaries, so they get packaged and sent straight into the lymphatic lacteals instead!

question: Which nervous system response directly triggers a penile erection?

options.A: Parasympathetic stimulation
options.B: Sympathetic vasoconstriction
options.C: Enteric nervous inhibition
options.D: Somatic reflex suppression

explanation: Parasympathetic nerve signals cause blood vessels in the erectile tissue to dilate, allowing blood to fill the spaces. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is the primary physiological defect in Type 1 diabetes mellitus?

options.A: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells
options.B: Peripheral resistance to the action of insulin
options.C: Temporary glucose intolerance during pregnancy
options.D: Excessive production of glucagon by the liver

explanation: Type 1 diabetes occurs when the immune system mistakenly attacks and destroys the insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h1)

question: A patient suddenly loses their job and becomes homeless. Which category of health determinants is mainly at play here?

options.A: Biological determinants
options.B: Social and environmental determinants
options.C: Genetic determinants
options.D: Neurochemical determinants

explanation: You got it! Things like a stable job, housing, and financial security belong to our social and environmental surroundings, which heavily influence our peace of mind.

question: What is the primary reason for performing meticulous pin site care on a patient with skeletal traction?

options.A: To encourage faster healing of torn skin ligaments
options.B: To keep the traction weights from touching the floor
options.C: To stop the metal pins from slipping out of the bone
options.D: To prevent dangerous bone infections like osteomyelitis

explanation: Pin sites create a direct open route from the environment to the bone, making rigorous sterile cleaning vital to stop bacterial invasion. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T7#GNS221_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is a major bottleneck when trying to execute the Nigerian health budget?

options.A: Delayed release of approved funds by treasury authorities
options.B: Excessive availability of cash at the primary clinic level
options.C: Automatic approval of all health sector requests
options.D: Complete absence of legislative review

explanation: Even when a budget looks great on paper, getting the actual cash released to clinics often takes a frustratingly long time.

question: Which of these is a major duty of the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare?

options.A: Building commercial real estate for private citizens
options.B: Issuing traffic tickets in major cities
options.C: Collecting personal income taxes from workers
options.D: Formulating national health policies and setting clinical standards

explanation: You got it! The federal ministry sets the big-picture rules and clinical standards that guide healthcare practice all across Nigeria.

question: Which part of the reflex arc carries the electrical signal away from the spinal cord to the target muscle or gland?

options.A: Integration center
options.B: Sensory neuron
options.C: Sensory receptor
options.D: Motor neuron

explanation: Think of the motor neuron as the outgoing mail carrier. It takes the processed signal from the spinal cord out to the muscle so it knows to move!

question: Which landmark sits right between the front and back fontanelles on a baby's head?

options.A: The mentum
options.B: The vertex
options.C: The base
options.D: The face

explanation: You've got this! The vertex is simply the top part of the head, located right between the two main soft spots (fontanelles).

question: How does metabolic stress differ from simple starvation?

options.A: Metabolic stress lowers the heart rate to save body nutrients.
options.B: Metabolic stress forces high energy use while blocking normal tissue conservation.
options.C: Simple starvation causes sudden swelling all over the body.
options.D: Simple starvation causes a faster breakdown of muscle than major trauma.

explanation: While simple starvation triggers energy-saving mechanisms, inflammatory metabolic stress forces continuous tissue breakdown without letting the body conserve resources. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h3)

question: What is a major health risk when growing infants are denied protein-rich foods because of cultural myths?

options.A: Faster physical growth
options.B: Improved natural immunity
options.C: Stronger bone density
options.D: Malnutrition and stunting

explanation: Withholding essential building blocks like protein from growing children frequently leads to malnutrition and delayed physical growth. Good nutrition education changes lives here!

question: How should a clinical instructor react if a student makes a mistake during a practice simulation?

options.A: Punish the student publicly to scare others
options.B: Kick the student out of the nursing program right away
options.C: Use the mistake as a teaching moment for reflection
options.D: Pretend nothing happened so nobody feels bad

explanation: Mistakes are normal when learning! A good tutor turns an error into a helpful lesson without making you feel bad about yourself.

question: What is one major perk of condoms over hormonal birth control pills?

options.A: Condoms require no action at the time of intercourse
options.B: Condoms cause permanent changes in fertility
options.C: Condoms have a much higher real-world perfection rate
options.D: Condoms offer protection against sexually transmitted infections

explanation: You got it! While pills are great for preventing pregnancy, only barrier methods like condoms protect against STIs too.

question: Why must nurses carefully separate normal aging from disease pathology?

options.A: To prove that biological aging can be completely reversed with rest
options.B: To determine the exact financial cost of long-term hospital admission
options.C: To ensure that older adults never receive any prescription medications
options.D: To avoid treating normal age-related changes as if they are illnesses

explanation: Knowing what changes are a natural part of growing older prevents unnecessary medical interventions and helps nurses focus true care where it is needed. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T8#GNS225_U5_T8_h1)

question: What is the main goal of food budgeting in clinical nutrition?

options.A: To plan food spending without compromising nutritional health
options.B: To buy only the cheapest food available on the market
options.C: To eliminate all spending on processed and convenience foods
options.D: To calculate the exact daily calorie intake of a patient

explanation: Spot on! Food budgeting is all about balancing your pocket with your plate so you never have to sacrifice good health just to save some cash. You've got this!

question: What do the letters SWOT stand for in healthcare management planning?

options.A: Safety, Wellness, Operations, Treatment
options.B: Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats
options.C: Staff, Workflows, Organization, Timing
options.D: Supervision, Wages, Output, Tasks

explanation: SWOT analysis evaluates internal strengths and weaknesses, and external opportunities and threats. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h5)

question: How do hydatid embryos first travel from the gut to organs like the liver?

options.A: Through the lymphatic drainage channels
options.B: Through the central nervous system pathways
options.C: By crawling directly through the abdominal wall
options.D: Through the portal venous system

explanation: After crossing the gut wall, they jump into blood vessels and ride the portal vein straight into the liver.

question: How does a secondary immune response compare to a primary immune response?

options.A: It produces only short-lived antibodies that cannot destroy viruses.
options.B: It relies entirely on innate barriers rather than white blood cells.
options.C: It causes severe clinical illness because the pathogen is stronger.
options.D: It is faster and produces a much larger amount of antibodies.

explanation: Because of memory cells, the secondary response acts fast and floods your system with antibodies to stop infections early.

question: A rural village uses its own communal labor and local materials to build a shade structure for an immunization clinic. Which objective does this best demonstrate?

options.A: Strict political control
options.B: Individual clinical diagnosis
options.C: External donor dependency
options.D: Resource mobilisation

explanation: Using local labour and materials to support a health project is a clear example of resource mobilisation from within the community. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h2)

question: You pick up a sterile tray and notice the outer wrap is damp. What should you do?

options.A: Dry the outer packaging with a clean paper towel and use it immediately
options.B: Open the pack and quickly wipe down the interior instruments with alcohol
options.C: Reject the tray and obtain a new one because moisture causes contamination
options.D: Place the pack back into the warming cabinet until the moisture evaporates

explanation: Wet packs are a no-go! Moisture lets germs soak straight through the paper wrap, contaminating the instruments inside.

question: What foods does the DASH diet mainly encourage patients to eat?

options.A: Red meats and refined white sugar
options.B: Fruits, vegetables, and low-fat dairy
options.C: Saturated fats and fried foods
options.D: High-sodium canned and processed meals

explanation: Spot on! The DASH diet focuses on whole foods packed with potassium, calcium, and magnesium to help keep blood pressure in check.

question: When the penis is resting (flaccid), what do the helical arteries do?

options.A: They pump high volumes of blood directly into the dorsal veins
options.B: They remain constricted to limit blood flow into the sinusoids
options.C: They provide somatic sensation to the skin of the penis
options.D: They actively secrete nitric oxide to maintain tissue relaxation

explanation: Well done! When resting, these arteries stay tightly clamped down so that only a small amount of blood enters.

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to teamwork across sectors in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive funding and immediate budget releases for all health programs
options.B: Sectoral sidelining and agencies operating in isolation
options.C: Bureaucratic red tape between different government tiers
options.D: Frequent changes in local political leadership

explanation: You got it! Chronic underfunding and delayed budgets are huge hurdles—we definitely don't have the problem of 'too much money'!

question: Which feature is essential for adolescent-friendly health services?

options.A: Higher service fees to cover specialized staff
options.B: Strict daytime-only scheduling constraints
options.C: Strict guarantee of client confidentiality
options.D: Mandatory parental presence during exams

explanation: Teens need to trust that their private health matters stay private. Confidentiality builds that crucial bridge!

question: What is the main responsibility of the supplementary motor area (SMA)?

options.A: Regulating baseline heart rate and breathing
options.B: Processing sharp pain and temperature sensations
options.C: Planning and sequencing complex movements
options.D: Translating spoken words into written text

explanation: You've got this! The SMA acts like a master planner, organizing movement sequences before you actually perform them.

question: What is the main target tissue of the somatic nervous system?

options.A: Endocrine glands
options.B: Skeletal muscle
options.C: Smooth muscle
options.D: Cardiac muscle

explanation: Correct! The somatic system controls your voluntary movements by talking directly to your skeletal muscles.

question: When wiping a bedside table in the ward, what direction should a nurse move?

options.A: From the cleanest area to the dirtiest area
options.B: Starting at the floor and moving upward
options.C: From the bottom edges up to the top center
options.D: In random circles across the entire surface

explanation: Smart nursing habit! Moving from clean to dirty ensures you aren't dragging grime and germs right back onto the spotless parts of the table.

question: Why are community health nurses often the first to spot developmental delays in children?

options.A: They perform all surgical procedures in the country
options.B: They interact with families regularly during home and clinic visits
options.C: They manage the national legal courts
options.D: They live in federal legislative offices

explanation: Because community health nurses visit homes and local clinics often, they are in the best position to notice early developmental milestones and red flags.

question: What physical property helps a drug cross a mucous membrane in a hurry?

options.A: Large molecular weight
options.B: High lipid solubility
options.C: Inability to dissolve in water
options.D: Strong acidic composition

explanation: Like dissolves like! Because cell membranes are made of fats (lipids), fat-loving (lipid-soluble) drugs slip right through them with ease.

question: What is the main medical goal of giving a patient a sitz bath?

options.A: To lower a very high fever using freezing cold water
options.B: To increase joint flexibility in patients with severe arthritis
options.C: To reduce pain and swelling in the perineal and rectal area
options.D: To scrub off dead skin cells from the entire body surface

explanation: You've got this! A sitz bath focuses warm water right on the lower trunk to soothe discomfort from things like hemorrhoids or childbirth.

question: Why is it actually helpful for bedside nurses to understand basic health economics?

options.A: It helps them appreciate the operational challenges of resource allocation and patient flow
options.B: It prevents patients from ever experiencing chronic illnesses in the community
options.C: It allows them to negotiate direct commission fees for prescribing medications
options.D: It removes the need for doctors to write formal treatment orders

explanation: Spot on! Knowing economics helps you understand why management makes certain staffing decisions and how best to manage patient beds on your ward.

question: Which heart chamber pumps deoxygenated blood into the pulmonary trunk?

options.A: Right atrium
options.B: Right ventricle
options.C: Left atrium
options.D: Left ventricle

explanation: The right ventricle is responsible for forcing deoxygenated blood out of the heart and into the pulmonary trunk toward the lungs. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to getting contraceptives in Nigeria?

options.A: Geographic distance to the nearest healthcare center
options.B: Stockouts of essential commodities at health facilities
options.C: Judgmental attitudes from healthcare workers
options.D: Universal availability of free home-delivery services

explanation: Correct! Free home delivery is not a standard reality across Nigeria. Instead, long distances, running out of supplies, and unfriendly attitudes are the real challenges clients face.

question: Why shouldn't you treat an undiagnosed megaloblastic anemia with just folic acid?

options.A: It destroys all existing platelets in the bloodstream
options.B: It permanently stops iron absorption in the stomach
options.C: It can mask B12 deficiency while nerve damage worsens
options.D: It immediately causes complete liver failure

explanation: Folic acid can make the blood look better while secretly letting B12 nerve damage continue to progress silently. Always check the root cause!

question: On a busy hospital ward, what is the most common reason medication preparation errors happen?

options.A: Patients refusing to take bitter-tasting liquids
options.B: Pharmacies sending drugs in alphabetical order
options.C: Lack of basic mathematical formulas in textbooks
options.D: Distractions and interruptions during the setup process

explanation: Interruptions break your concentration easily. That's why creating a quiet zone for yourself during drug prep is such a great nursing habit!

question: Why does the electrical signal pause briefly at the AV node before heading down to the ventricles?

options.A: To let the heart take a quick rest between beats
options.B: To send extra blood back up into the lungs
options.C: To give the ventricles enough time to fill completely with blood
options.D: To measure the exact blood pressure inside the atria

explanation: That tiny pause is super important! It ensures the top chambers (atria) finish squeezing all their blood down into the bottom chambers before the ventricles pump it away.

question: A community nurse notices that an elderly client's primary caregiver looks extremely exhausted and frustrated. What is the best way to document this observation?

options.A: Record specific behavioral signs of fatigue in the caregiver and note the risk of burnout
options.B: Write that the family member is lazy and refuses to help the sick client
options.C: Document that the home environment is completely peaceful and supportive
options.D: Ignore the observation because the family member is not the official client

explanation: Documenting caregiver strain objectively helps the healthcare team plan interventions to support the family and protect the client. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which injection site is generally considered the safest for adult patients?

options.A: Deltoid
options.B: Dorsogluteal
options.C: Ventrogluteal
options.D: Vastus lateralis

explanation: The ventrogluteal site lacks major nerves and large blood vessels, making it the preferred and safest choice for adults. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h2)

question: Which lifestyle habit directly damages blood vessels and is a major cause of sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Cigarette smoking
options.B: Eating fresh green vegetables
options.C: Walking briskly every morning
options.D: Drinking too much clean water

explanation: Smoking harms blood vessel walls and reduces blood flow all over the body, which heavily impacts sexual function.

question: What is the main goal of a public-private partnership (PPP) in healthcare?

options.A: To combine government resources with private sector investment and efficiency
options.B: To ensure that private companies take full control of national health policy
options.C: To completely transfer government health responsibilities to private owners
options.D: To eliminate all out-of-pocket costs for vulnerable patient populations

explanation: Think of a PPP as teamwork! The government teams up with private companies to bring in extra funds and better management, making health systems stronger together.

question: You are caring for a mother 2 hours after delivery. Which finding needs your immediate action?

options.A: Moderate fatigue and sleepiness following labor
options.B: Mild cramping pains while the baby is breastfeeding
options.C: A rapidly filling perineal pad with bright red blood
options.D: A temperature of 37.2 degrees Celsius

explanation: Well done! Heavy, soaking bleeding is a sign of postpartum hemorrhage—a true emergency that needs quick nursing intervention.

question: What is a major risk if a patient stops taking their antibiotics early because they start feeling better?

options.A: The body will stop making white blood cells
options.B: The infection can return stronger and cause long-term damage
options.C: The ovaries will immediately double in size
options.D: The patient will instantly develop kidney failure

explanation: Always educate your patients to finish their drugs! Stopping early leaves the toughest bacteria alive to bounce back harder and cause scarring.

question: Why do many patients with chronic kidney disease end up developing anemia?

options.A: The spleen removes healthy blood cells prematurely
options.B: The body destroys red blood cells too quickly
options.C: Dietary iron is no longer absorbed in the gut
options.D: Damaged kidneys fail to produce enough erythropoietin

explanation: You're learning fast! Since sick kidneys can't make enough EPO, the bone marrow doesn't get the signal to build new red blood cells, leading to anemia.

question: A patient says they want to save half their leftover antibiotics for a family member who might fall sick later. How should you respond?

options.A: Explain the dangers of sharing medications and encourage proper disposal
options.B: Write down instructions on which family member should take the leftover pills
options.C: Advise the patient to double the dose next time someone coughs
options.D: Praise the patient for being resourceful and saving money

explanation: Wonderful! As a nurse, you want to warmly educate patients on why sharing drugs spreads resistance and toxicity.

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse needs to teach a patient recovering from a hysteroscopic polyp removal?

options.A: Reporting fever or worsening pelvic pain
options.B: Understanding when sexual activity can safely resume
options.C: How to perform daily abdominal wound dressing changes
options.D: Recognizing signs of heavy vaginal bleeding

explanation: Correct! Because hysteroscopy is done entirely through the natural passages (vagina and cervix), there are no abdominal cuts or dressings to worry about.

question: What do we mean by 'psychological safety' in a nursing unit?

options.A: The mandatory wearing of protective equipment
options.B: The physical security of staff against outside intruders
options.C: The freedom to speak up about safety concerns without fear
options.D: The absence of stressful patients in the ward

explanation: Exactly! Psychological safety means you can ask questions or report a worry without stressing about being yelled at or victimized by colleagues.

question: Why is it important to encourage a laboring mother to empty her bladder often?

options.A: Urine samples must be tested every hour during home births
options.B: It stops the uterus from contracting too strongly
options.C: It prevents the development of chronic urinary tract infections
options.D: A full bladder can obstruct fetal descent and slow down labor

explanation: Think of the bladder like a roadblock in the pelvis! Emptying it clears the way so the baby's head can move down smoothly.

question: What is an important feature of the data you get from using the sisterhood method?

options.A: It focuses exclusively on deaths caused by non-communicable chronic diseases.
options.B: It measures the exact number of live births occurring in rural clinics.
options.C: It provides a retrospective estimate reflecting mortality over the past several years.
options.D: It gives real-time daily updates of maternal deaths in tertiary hospitals.

explanation: Because people are remembering events over their sisters' entire lives, the results give us a useful average look back at past years, rather than just today's numbers.

question: What is your very first action if a surgical drain accidentally falls completely out of a patient's wound?

options.A: Try to gently push the same tube right back into the hole
options.B: Leave the open wound uncovered so fresh air can dry it out
options.C: Cover the open site with a sterile dressing and notify the doctor
options.D: Wash the fallen tube with soap and tape it back onto the skin

explanation: Never try to push a fallen drain back in—that introduces germs! Instead, cover the site with a sterile dressing right away and call the doctor.

question: Why does Primary Health Care require different sectors to work together (intersectoral collaboration)?

options.A: Because the Ministry of Health cannot legally purchase medications without other ministries
options.B: Because doctors need assistance from foreign engineers to run rural clinics
options.C: Because health is influenced by non-medical factors like education, agriculture, and clean water
options.D: Because nurses are required to work in agricultural fields during planting seasons

explanation: Well done! Good health goes beyond medicine. It relies heavily on food security, safe water, and education—which means different government sectors must team up.

question: What do we call the large amount of urine passed in the first few days after having a baby?

options.A: Tubular necrosis
options.B: Glomerular shutdown
options.C: Postpartum diuresis
options.D: Renal exhaustion

explanation: Postpartum diuresis is just the body's way of getting rid of all that extra pregnancy fluid it doesn't need anymore. Frequent trips to the bathroom are expected!

question: What happens if a traction rope slips out of its pulley groove?

options.A: The patient's blood pressure will drop rapidly
options.B: The pulling force on the extremity is lost
options.C: The fracture will heal twice as fast
options.D: Skin breakdown will immediately disappear

explanation: If the rope rubs against the bed frame instead of the pulley, the mechanical pull stops and the traction won't work. Good thing you're checking your equipment!

question: Which of these is an objective measurement nurses use during a nutritional assessment?

options.A: How many meals the patient ate as a child
options.B: The patient's favorite cultural food dishes
options.C: The patient's personal opinion on their appetite
options.D: Body mass index and laboratory blood panels

explanation: Spot on! Objective data means measurable facts—like BMI and lab results—rather than just guessing based on what someone tells you.

question: What is a pathological fracture?

options.A: A break caused by a disease that has weakened the bone structure
options.B: A fracture that occurs strictly from a high-speed vehicle crash
options.C: A bone injury that happens exclusively during heavy contact sports
options.D: A hairline crack that cannot be seen on a standard X-ray image

explanation: Think of conditions like osteoporosis or tumors. They weaken bones so much that even normal, everyday movements can cause a break without any major accident happening.

question: Which antibiotic is commonly prescribed first-line for animal and human bite injuries?

options.A: Erythromycin ointment
options.B: Ciprofloxacin drops
options.C: Amoxicillin-clavulanate
options.D: Vancomycin syrup

explanation: Amoxicillin-clavulanate is a great choice because it covers the wide variety of bacteria typically found lurking in human and animal mouths.

question: You are caring for an unconscious patient with a severe brain injury. Which nursing action best prevents aspiration?

options.A: Removing all oral secretions using a tongue blade
options.B: Laying the patient flat on their back to rest
options.C: Keeping the head of the bed elevated at 30 to 45 degrees
options.D: Feeding small pureed meals every two hours

explanation: Gravity is your friend here! Elevating the bed stops stomach contents and saliva from flowing back into the lungs.

question: What is the main goal when a patient arrives in the emergency department?

options.A: To provide long-term rehabilitation therapy
options.B: To discharge patients within a strict time limit
options.C: To complete detailed medical histories for all patients
options.D: To stabilize life-threatening conditions swiftly

explanation: Spot on! In emergency nursing, the absolute priority is making sure the patient stays alive and stable before worrying about anything else. You're doing great!

question: A patient with new hearing aids complains that everyday sounds are way too loud and annoying. What should you tell them?

options.A: Advise the patient to stop wearing the hearing aids permanently
options.B: Explain that the brain needs time to adjust to amplified environmental sounds
options.C: Tell the patient to turn the volume control up even higher for clarity
options.D: Acknowledge that the device is broken and needs immediate replacement

explanation: It's totally normal! When someone hasn't heard everyday sounds clearly in a while, their brain gets overwhelmed at first. Give it time and patience.

question: What type of medication must be given for a few weeks before surgery to remove a pheochromocytoma?

options.A: Alpha-blockers
options.B: Potassium supplements
options.C: Insulin infusions
options.D: Corticosteroids

explanation: Before surgeons touch a pheochromocytoma, the patient needs alpha-blockers to keep their blood vessels relaxed and prevent dangerous blood pressure spikes during the operation.

question: What is the main purpose of a Root Cause Analysis (RCA)?

options.A: To assign blame and punishment to negligent staff members
options.B: To calculate the financial cost of patient lawsuits
options.C: To investigate why an error occurred by identifying underlying system flaws
options.D: To evaluate the daily bedside performance of individual students

explanation: RCA is like detective work! It looks deep into the system to find out why a mistake happened, rather than just pointing fingers at a person.

question: Why do health guidelines look closely at the *type* of fat we eat, rather than just total grams?

options.A: The body cannot digest saturated fats at all
options.B: Unsaturated fats provide zero energy
options.C: Different fats have very different effects on heart health
options.D: Total fat intake has no effect on body weight

explanation: Not all fats are enemies! While trans fats clog arteries, healthy fats like olive oil protect your heart. It's all about quality over quantity.

question: A community health nurse is teaching villagers how Ebola spreads. Which practice should she warn against the most?

options.A: Drinking boiled water from a community well during dry seasons
options.B: Eating well-cooked pork from certified local livestock farms
options.C: Washing the body of a relative who died from suspected Ebola
options.D: Sharing eating utensils with a family member who has malaria

explanation: Well done! The viral load is super high in someone who just passed away, making traditional burial touching very risky.

question: Why is psychological safety so important for nurses on the ward?

options.A: It allows nurses to skip mandatory documentation and charting duties
options.B: It gives them the confidence to speak up about safety hazards without fear
options.C: It completely eliminates all physical stress and burnout on the ward
options.D: It prevents patients from asking difficult questions about their care

explanation: When nurses feel psychologically safe, they won't hesitate to question a dodgy doctor's order or report a near-miss, and that saves lives!

question: How high should an infant's bottom be from the mattress in Gallows traction?

options.A: Lifted just barely so a hand can slide underneath
options.B: Raised at least twelve inches high
options.C: Tilted completely sideways
options.D: Pressed firmly against the mattress

explanation: Just a tiny lift is the magic trick! It uses the baby's own upper body weight to create the counter-pulling force.

question: Which table design is most preferred in modern academic writing?

options.A: Few horizontal lines and no vertical lines
options.B: Bright neon colors to highlight important rows
options.C: Thick black borders around every single cell
options.D: Randomly placed gridlines for visual excitement

explanation: Modern tables keep it clean and professional by ditching heavy vertical borders and using only a few horizontal lines.

question: What is the main job of the body's modulation phase in the pain pathway?

options.A: Deciding the emotional meaning of the injury in the brain
options.B: Converting tissue injury into a nerve impulse
options.C: Releasing natural body chemicals to turn down the pain signal
options.D: Carrying the electrical message up the spinal cord

explanation: Think of modulation as your body's built-in volume control! It releases substances like endorphins right in the spinal cord to quiet down the pain message.

question: What kind of container must you always use to throw away used needles and blades?

options.A: Puncture-resistant safety boxes
options.B: Open woven baskets with plastic liners
options.C: Standard cardboard shipping cartons
options.D: Black municipal garbage bags

explanation: Spot on! Sharps need hard, sturdy containers so needles can't poke right through the sides and injure someone.

question: Why is final reporting to the community an essential final step?

options.A: To prove to the government that the nurses deserve a salary raise
options.B: To fulfill a legal requirement so nurses can travel abroad
options.C: To advertise private clinics opening in nearby towns
options.D: To maintain transparency and respect for community participation

explanation: Feeding results back to the community shows respect, maintains trust, and encourages continued community-driven health maintenance. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h7)

question: Where in the body are the main arterial pressure sensors (baroreceptors) located?

options.A: Pulmonary veins and left ventricle
options.B: Renal cortex and medullary pyramids
options.C: Carotid sinuses and aortic arch
options.D: Right atrium and superior vena cava

explanation: The body keeps tabs on blood pressure using special stretch sensors placed right near the brain's highway (carotid sinuses) and the main exit from the heart (aortic arch).

question: A patient has widespread body pain, tender points, and ongoing fatigue, but no visible joint swelling. What condition fits best?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.B: Osteoarthritis
options.C: Fibromyalgia
options.D: Gout

explanation: Fibromyalgia is known for widespread pain and tender points, but unlike arthritis, it doesn't cause joint swelling or deformity. Great to keep this distinction in mind!

question: What is the main benefit of combining both primary and secondary data sources?

options.A: It allows the nurse to finish community work without visiting the field
options.B: It prevents community members from asking questions about healthcare
options.C: It gives a balanced and realistic view of local health realities by cross-checking facts
options.D: It guarantees that government funding will double immediately

explanation: Using multiple sources helps verify findings and provides a thorough picture of community health status. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h3)

question: What does a pacemaker 'failure to capture' mean?

options.A: Pacing spikes show on the monitor, but the heart does not beat in response
options.B: The device fails to notice the patient's own heartbeat and fires at the wrong time
options.C: The wires disconnect from the skin surface outside the chest wall
options.D: The internal battery runs out completely and the heart stops instantly

explanation: Failure to capture means the pacemaker is sending out the signal (the spike), but the heart muscle isn't responding to it. You are getting the hang of ECG concepts!

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluation in public health projects?

options.A: Monitoring costs a lot of money, while evaluation is completely free
options.B: Monitoring is done only by doctors, while evaluation is done by patients
options.C: Monitoring is continuous tracking, while evaluation measures final outcomes against objectives
options.D: Monitoring focuses on finance, while evaluation focuses entirely on building roads

explanation: Monitoring happens all through the project to keep things on track, whereas evaluation looks back to see if goals were met. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h9)

question: What is the first crucial step before collecting data in a new community?

options.A: Writing a final report for the federal ministry of health
options.B: Administering mass vaccinations to all children under five
options.C: Demolishing illegal structures that block drainage systems
options.D: Community entry and gaining the trust of local leaders

explanation: Without properly introducing the team to local leaders and gaining entry, residents may be uncooperative and data collection will fail. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why do we put healthy-feeling people into quarantine after a known exposure to a contagious illness?

options.A: To monitor them through the incubation period before they can spread the disease asymptomatically
options.B: To punish individuals who failed to maintain proper personal hygiene standards
options.C: To immediately administer therapeutic antibiotics regardless of the actual pathogen involved
options.D: To provide them with active immunity through immediate vaccination in a controlled facility

explanation: Spot on! It catches sneaky infections early so they don't pass them on to others before showing symptoms.

question: What happens to the spread of disease if a nurse successfully breaks even one link in the chain of infection?

options.A: The pathogen automatically changes into a harmless bacteria
options.B: The patient develops instant immunity against all other germs
options.C: The infection cycle is stopped and disease spread is prevented
options.D: The reservoir completely disappears from the environment

explanation: Because the chain requires every single link to function, breaking just one link halts the entire transmission process. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which learning theory looks mostly at outward actions and how rewards or corrections shape them?

options.A: Cognitivism
options.B: Humanism
options.C: Constructivism
options.D: Behaviorism

explanation: Behaviorism is all about stimulus and response—like praising a child for good behavior or correcting a mistake so it doesn't happen again.

question: What is a key nursing duty when checking a pregnant patient's skin?

options.A: Differentiating harmless body changes from serious medical conditions
options.B: Telling the patient to ignore any skin changes until after delivery
options.C: Reporting all common stretch marks to the primary surgeon
options.D: Prescribing strong steroid creams to cure all rashes instantly

explanation: You are the frontline! Knowing the difference between normal pregnancy glow-ups and warning signs like cholestasis makes you an awesome nurse.

question: Why does a hospital ward have separate clean utility and dirty utility rooms?

options.A: To comply with fire safety evacuation rules
options.B: To give nurses a private space to take meal breaks
options.C: To separate male patients from female patients
options.D: To prevent cross-contamination between sterile supplies and waste

explanation: Separation ensures clean medical supplies do not mix with used equipment, body fluids, or waste items. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why is a nurse's daily report on how much a patient ate so helpful to the dietitian?

options.A: It allows the nurse to prescribe new therapeutic diets alone
options.B: It replaces the need for laboratory blood test investigations
options.C: It helps the dietitian evaluate if nutritional targets are met
options.D: It determines the daily work schedule of the kitchen staff

explanation: Exactly! Nurses are at the bedside every day, so tracking actual meal intake helps the whole team know if the patient is getting enough nourishment.

question: Why would a doctor choose a tracheostomy instead of keeping a breathing tube through the mouth long-term?

options.A: It completely stops any risk of getting an infection
options.B: It means you never have to clean around the site or use suction
options.C: It is much more comfortable and safer for long-term breathing support
options.D: It is much faster to do in an outdoor emergency

explanation: Having a tube taped through the mouth for weeks can damage the vocal cords and mouth. A tracheostomy provides a secure, comfortable airway right through the neck for patients who need long-term help.

question: Why must nurses always ask patients if they are taking traditional or herbal remedies along with prescribed drugs?

options.A: To calculate the patient's daily fluid intake and output accurately
options.B: To prevent dangerous herb-drug interactions that could harm the patient
options.C: To prove that orthodox medicine is superior to cultural treatments
options.D: To report traditional healers to the local pharmaceutical board

explanation: Herbs are powerful! Mixing them with hospital medications can cause bad reactions or stop the prescribed drug from working.

question: Why are accurate meeting minutes considered important legal records in healthcare?

options.A: They serve as proof of staff attendance for annual salary increases
options.B: They provide a clear audit trail of accountability and quality improvement decisions
options.C: They act as marketing material for prospective nursing students
options.D: They replace the need for patient clinical chart documentation

explanation: Minutes show that the facility actively addressed safety and operational issues over time.

question: Why would an occupational health nurse test the hearing of workers in a noisy textile mill?

options.A: To identify early signs of noise-induced hearing loss before it worsens
options.B: To check if employees are listening to unauthorized radio stations
options.C: To measure how fast the machinery is producing textile materials
options.D: To test the general intelligence and problem-solving skills of the staff

explanation: Loud factory noise can slowly damage hearing over time. Regular hearing tests (audiometry) help us catch any small changes early so we can protect the workers' ears.

question: What type of receptors do smell molecules (odorants) bind to on the tiny hairs in our nose?

options.A: Voltage-gated calcium channels
options.B: Ligand-gated mechanical pores
options.C: G-protein coupled receptors
options.D: Steroid hormone receptors

explanation: You're doing great! Odorants lock into special G-protein coupled receptors on the olfactory cilia, triggering a chemical cascade that lets our brain know we're smelling something.

question: Why is it so important for the local community to actively take part in health programs?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to visit households in remote villages
options.B: It eliminates the need for any financial support from the federal ministry
options.C: It legally binds the local government to fund the health center indefinitely
options.D: It ensures that projects address real local needs and encourages people to maintain them

explanation: Exactly! When community members help plan a project, they feel a sense of ownership and are much more likely to keep it running successfully.

question: How does continuous on-the-job training help primary healthcare workers?

options.A: It ensures that health workers never experience professional burnout
options.B: It automatically increases the monthly budgetary allocation of the facility
options.C: It replaces the need for basic professional nursing education entirely
options.D: It keeps workers updated on new protocols and improves clinical confidence

explanation: Regular training boosts your confidence and makes sure you are up-to-date with the latest and best ways to care for your patients.

question: What is the main difference between skilled care and custodial care?

options.A: Skilled care requires licensed health professionals for complex medical needs.
options.B: Custodial care is only provided inside large acute care hospitals.
options.C: Custodial care requires advanced clinical judgment and monitoring.
options.D: Skilled care focuses exclusively on helping residents bathe and dress.

explanation: You've got this! Skilled care is all about medical tasks done by trained pros, while custodial care helps with everyday living activities like bathing. Great job keeping them straight!

question: Which two body systems are most commonly hit hardest by inherited degenerative disorders?

options.A: Gastrointestinal and renal systems
options.B: Hematopoietic and lymphatic systems
options.C: Endocrine and integumentary systems
options.D: Nervous system and muscles

explanation: Think about movement and thinking! These genetic conditions mainly target our nerves and muscles as they progress.

question: Why do doctors usually choose levothyroxine over other options for thyroid replacement?

options.A: It contains both active and inactive hormones in variable amounts
options.B: It has a predictable potency and smooth onset of action
options.C: It is derived directly from animal thyroid glands
options.D: It acts much faster than synthetic triiodothyronine

explanation: Levothyroxine is lab-made and gives a steady, reliable daily dose. No nasty surprises or wild hormone spikes!

question: A seventy-year-old patient is losing muscle mass and experiencing bone weakness. Which adjustment is most important to emphasize in their daily meal plan?

options.A: Strict reduction of all dietary fats and oils
options.B: Significantly increased total daily caloric intake
options.C: Elimination of all complex carbohydrates
options.D: Higher amounts of protein, vitamin D, and calcium

explanation: Older adults need adequate protein to fight muscle loss and calcium with vitamin D to maintain bone strength despite lower overall calorie needs. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h2)

question: A patient tells you that both of their parents have high blood pressure and diabetes. Where should you write this?

options.A: Past medical history
options.B: History of present illness
options.C: Review of systems
options.D: Family history

explanation: Spot on! Information about blood relatives (like parents and siblings) always goes into the family history section so you can check for genetic risks.

question: What is the primary mode of transmission for Mycobacterium tuberculosis?

options.A: Airborne droplets from infected individuals
options.B: Vector-borne transmission through mosquito bites
options.C: Direct contact with contaminated skin wounds
options.D: Ingestion of unpasteurized dairy products

explanation: TB bacteria spread through the air when a person with active disease coughs or sneezes, allowing others to inhale the droplets into their lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h1)

question: What is the typical length of a normal menstrual cycle for an adult woman?

options.A: 40 to 50 days
options.B: 60 to 75 days
options.C: 21 to 35 days
options.D: 10 to 14 days

explanation: While textbooks love talking about a 28-day cycle, any cycle that consistently falls between 21 and 35 days is completely normal and healthy!

question: Why is it important to run physical medical tests on someone presenting with severe anxiety symptoms?

options.A: To determine the correct dosage of psychotherapy immediately
options.B: To measure the exact concentration of brain neurotransmitters
options.C: To rule out medical conditions like hyperthyroidism that mimic anxiety
options.D: To prove that the patient is faking psychological distress

explanation: Spot on! Conditions like an overactive thyroid can cause a racing pulse and tremors that look just like anxiety. We always check the physical body first!

question: What is a major root cause of unwanted pregnancies that lead to unsafe abortions?

options.A: Universal access to emergency birth control pills
options.B: Unmet needs and lack of access to modern contraceptives
options.C: Mandatory sex education classes in all primary schools
options.D: Excessive availability of free family planning clinics

explanation: When people cannot get or afford reliable birth control, unplanned pregnancies happen more often. Patient education is our best tool here!

question: A nurse is writing an introduction for a study on hand hygiene. What is the main goal of this section?

options.A: Summarizing the final statistical data collected from the hospital wards
options.B: Establishing the gap in current compliance knowledge and stating study aims
options.C: Providing personal opinions on why hospital staff refuse to wash hands
options.D: Listing every historical discovery of microscopic bacteria since the nineteenth century

explanation: The introduction sets the stage by showing what we already know, what is missing, and why this study is so important.

question: Which patient should be extra careful to avoid heavy straining and the Valsalva maneuver?

options.A: A patient with a mild cold or runny nose
options.B: A patient diagnosed with mild iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: A patient recovering from a recent heart attack (myocardial infarction)
options.D: A patient doing therapy for a sprained ankle

explanation: Straining spikes blood pressure and heart strain. For a patient healing from a heart attack, that extra stress can be very dangerous. Good clinical thinking!

question: Why is it a mistake to wipe a chemical disinfectant off a surface immediately after spraying it?

options.A: Leaving it wet makes the table look shiny and polished to visitors
options.B: The chemical needs a specific contact time to successfully kill the germs
options.C: The cleaning cloth will instantly dissolve if it touches wet disinfectant
options.D: Quick drying causes the chemical to release poisonous gases into the room

explanation: Disinfectants require time to act against pathogens; wiping them away prematurely prevents complete disinfection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why is insulin considered the preferred medication for managing diabetes during pregnancy?

options.A: It does not cross the placenta in significant amounts
options.B: It stimulates the placenta to produce less growth hormone
options.C: It cures the underlying pancreatic beta-cell defect permanently
options.D: It can be taken orally instead of through painful injections

explanation: Insulin is a large protein molecule that does not readily cross the placental barrier, making it safe for the developing fetus while lowering maternal blood sugar. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h5)

question: Why do nurses closely monitor blood potassium levels in patients taking loop diuretics?

options.A: Loop diuretics cause the body to lose potassium in the urine
options.B: Potassium prevents the patient from developing a dry cough
options.C: Potassium levels determine the correct dose of furosemide
options.D: High potassium levels stop the diuretic from working completely

explanation: Spot on! Loop diuretics flush out water, but they drag important potassium along with it. Keeping an eye on labs helps us prevent dangerous low potassium (hypokalemia).

question: In an emergency, when would a nurse use a defibrillator?

options.A: To slow down a fast heart rate caused by a mild fever
options.B: To restart a heart that already has a normal, healthy rhythm
options.C: To check the electrical resistance of the chest skin
options.D: To stop dangerous, chaotic heart rhythms like ventricular fibrillation

explanation: A defibrillator delivers a quick shock to pause chaotic electrical activity so the heart's natural pacemaker can take over again. Lifesaving nursing knowledge!

question: Which legal concept allows nurses and doctors to treat an unconscious emergency patient without explicit consent?

options.A: Res ipsa loquitur
options.B: Emergency privilege
options.C: Vicarious liability
options.D: Professional indemnity

explanation: Correct! Emergency privilege assumes a patient would want life-saving care when they are unable to speak for themselves.

question: After giving a patient pain medication through an IV, when is the best time for a nurse to check if it worked?

options.A: 15 to 30 minutes later
options.B: 6 to 8 hours later
options.C: At the end of the shift
options.D: 2 to 4 hours later

explanation: IV medications enter the bloodstream immediately, so you should check back in 15 to 30 minutes to make sure the pain is going down safely.

question: In what year was the VAPP Act passed into law in Nigeria to protect people against violence?
explanation: Spot on! The VAPP Act was enacted in May 2015 to give survivors a strong legal backing against domestic violence and abuse.

question: Why must a pregnant woman report blurred vision and a terrible headache immediately?

options.A: They mean the mother needs stronger reading glasses
options.B: They are common signs of normal hormonal adjustment
options.C: They show that the baby is moving too much inside
options.D: They indicate severe high blood pressure or pre-eclampsia

explanation: Headaches and changes in vision are classic warning signs of dangerously high blood pressure. Catching pre-eclampsia early saves lives!

question: Your patient started a new drug and now has yellow eyes, dark urine, and tummy pain on the upper right side. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: A normal, expected side effect of starting antibiotic therapy
options.B: An idiosyncratic liver reaction to the new drug
options.C: An acute kidney injury caused by dehydration
options.D: A simple skin allergy triggered by sunlight

explanation: Yellow eyes (jaundice) and dark urine are classic red flags for drug-induced liver trouble. Great clinical spotting!

question: What happens to a weight measurement if a mechanical scale is placed on a thick carpeted floor?

options.A: The reading will be falsely lower than normal
options.B: The reading will be falsely higher than normal
options.C: The scale will lock and refuse to move
options.D: The scale will automatically calibrate itself

explanation: Carpet absorbs some of the downward force from the body, causing the scale to register less weight than the patient actually has. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h3)

question: As a community health nurse, what is a key duty when preparing for disasters?

options.A: Breaking down emergency guidelines into simple steps for residents
options.B: Managing the national budget for disaster relief
options.C: Building storm shelters and reinforced concrete walls
options.D: Declaring a formal state of emergency in the region

explanation: Great job! Nurses act as a bridge, turning complex disaster plans into clear, everyday steps that everyone can easily follow.

question: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of poor specimen collection technique?

options.A: Prescription of incorrect antibiotics
options.B: Need for painful repeat sample collection
options.C: Immediate cure of the bacterial infection
options.D: Inaccurate laboratory test results

explanation: Bad collection leads to wrong results and wrong drugs, which makes the infection drag on—it definitely won't cure it!

question: When is a formative evaluation done during an IEC program?

options.A: While nurses are writing hospital financial reports
options.B: Before the program starts, to test messages and materials
options.C: As an emergency response to a sudden disease outbreak
options.D: Only after all health campaigns have permanently ended

explanation: Think of formative evaluation as 'forming' your plan—you test your posters and messages before launching to make sure they actually make sense to the community. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h7)

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand a patient's cultural background regarding health?

options.A: Culture completely prevents patients from experiencing chronic pain.
options.B: Culture shapes how clients interpret symptoms and choose where to seek care.
options.C: Culture determines the exact medical dosage a patient's liver can metabolize.
options.D: Culture is the single biological cause of all infectious diseases.

explanation: Great thinking! Culture heavily influences whether someone trusts modern medicine, traditional healing, or a mix of both when they feel sick.

question: Which of these is a critical warning sign that a patient with an ovarian cyst should report right away?

options.A: A slight increase in clear vaginal discharge
options.B: Mild bloating right before her monthly period
options.C: Sudden, severe, and worsening abdominal pain
options.D: Feeling tired after a long day at work

explanation: Severe pain that comes out of nowhere is a red flag for dangerous complications like a cyst bursting or twisting (torsion). Always take it seriously!

question: What protective action prevents food from entering the respiratory airway during a normal swallow?

options.A: The tongue pushes forward to close off the esophagus
options.B: The vocal cords tighten to block all airflow permanently
options.C: The epiglottis folds down to cover the larynx
options.D: The hard palate drops down to seal the pharynx

explanation: During swallowing, the epiglottis acts like a lid, flipping downward to shield the airway and guide food safely into the esophagus. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why are regular joint simulation drills important before a disaster happens?

options.A: They replace the need for community involvement in healthcare delivery
options.B: They allow agencies to practice working together and find plan flaws
options.C: They guarantee that natural disasters will completely bypass the region
options.D: They reduce the annual budgetary allocation required for security forces

explanation: Practice makes perfect! Simulations let different teams test their teamwork and fix mistakes before a real emergency occurs.

question: A nurse wears gloves while emptying a patient's urinary catheter bag. Which link in the chain of infection is the nurse primarily trying to break?

options.A: Reservoir
options.B: Infectious agent
options.C: Mode of transmission
options.D: Susceptible host

explanation: Wearing gloves creates a barrier that stops germs from moving from the urine to the nurse's hands and onto other surfaces or patients. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is a common trap to avoid when designing a conceptual framework?

options.A: Sharing the research design with student nurses
options.B: Writing the framework on a white sheet of paper
options.C: Making the framework too complex and cluttered
options.D: Using too few words in the title of the study

explanation: Don't try to cram every single idea in the universe into one diagram! Keep it clean, simple, and testable.

question: Why is accurate nutritional documentation important among members of the healthcare team?

options.A: It replaces the need for verbal shift handovers entirely
options.B: It prevents the hospital from having to buy specialized nutritional supplements
options.C: It ensures clear communication between nurses, doctors, and dietitians for coordinated care
options.D: It is only used for insurance billing and has no role in clinical treatment

explanation: Clear notes allow every healthcare provider involved in the patient's care to understand their nutritional status and treatment plan. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h7)

question: Using the Plate Method for diabetes management, what should fill half of the dinner plate?

options.A: Full-fat dairy products
options.B: Starchy grains and yams
options.C: Lean protein foods
options.D: Non-starchy vegetables

explanation: Half of the plate should contain non-starchy vegetables to provide volume and fiber without raising blood sugar. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h4)

question: A nurse gives a patient pain medication. What is the best next step?

options.A: Instructing the patient to stop pressing the call bell
options.B: Documenting that the pain is completely gone forever
options.C: Reassessing the patient's pain level after a short interval
options.D: Discharging the patient immediately to save hospital beds

explanation: Always close the loop! Checking back in lets you know if the drug is actually doing its job or if the patient needs extra help.

question: If a patient sues a nurse for malpractice, what is the very first thing they must prove about their connection to the nurse?

options.A: That a professional duty of care existed between the nurse and patient
options.B: That the nurse intended to cause deliberate physical harm
options.C: That the hospital facility lacked an active accreditation
options.D: That the nurse was working past the scheduled shift time

explanation: Before a court can look at negligence, it must first be established that you were actually the nurse assigned to care for that patient—that's the duty of care!

question: Why is nebulization often chosen over other inhalers for patients in acute respiratory distress?

options.A: It requires only normal, quiet breathing instead of a deep, forced inhalation.
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any vital sign monitoring.
options.C: It stops all lung infections within minutes of starting the treatment.
